solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I defame a Sicilian perhaps

parts.note: to slander someone is to defame them

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to blackening the name of a man from Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Sicilian perhaps' is the definition: 'perhaps' warns that a Sicilian is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is an island, so anyone living there is an example of an island dweller.

clue.text: A commotion behind you and me

parts.note: the rump is the hindquarters, a behind
you and I together are us

explanation.surface: Somebody complains of a disturbance going on at their backs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' reads as a preposition but is the noun for one's bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or row, the same thing as a commotion.

clue.text: Expose Teddy, might one say?

indicators.note: asks what you would hear when the word is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear

explanation.surface: A question about whether to show off a cuddly toy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bare something is to uncover it and leave it open to view, that is to expose it.

clue.text: Notice article that makes you fume

explanation.surface: Spotting a certain newspaper piece leaves the reader furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe being inwardly angry, raging silently while barely containing temper.

clue.text: Margate's unlikely to become a name known to millions

indicators.note: something unlikely is improbable, so the place name must be turned into an improbable arrangement

parts.note: the Kent seaside town Margate plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: The modest English seaside town of Margate is hardly going to become world famous.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored, so the S of 'Margate's' joins the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is a hugely famous celebrity, whose name is recognised by enormous audiences everywhere.

clue.text: Delay robbery

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hitch that keeps things waiting
second meaning: an armed raid on a bank or coach

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a robbery being postponed; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a traffic or schedule hitch and a raid where victims are robbed at gunpoint.

clue.text: Two ambassadors causing outburst of amusement

wordplay.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador; two of them give it twice

explanation.surface: A pair of diplomats provokes laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated syllables imitate a giggle, the written sound of someone laughing at a joke.

clue.text: Cook uses Aga to make a bite to eat

indicators.note: to cook something is to tamper with it, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone prepares a snack on their Aga stove.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a big cast-iron range cooker found in many British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is a small meal or snack item, so it serves as an example of a bite to eat.

clue.text: Sneak off with east European, heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means travelling right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland

explanation.surface: Someone slips away with an eastern European who is travelling westward.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly with a lover, usually to marry, so to slip away unnoticed.

clue.text: Liberal MP getting stuck into booze

indicators.note: getting stuck into means plunging inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ale is beer, a kind of booze

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat politician enthusiastically drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the party of the MP, but it is the definition in its sense of generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean plentiful or given freely, as in a liberal helping, which matches abundant.

clue.text: Walk like a duck at start of trip? Rubbish!

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: ducks walk with a rolling, side-to-side gait

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of walking like a duck when setting off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are taken in reverse of their clue order: the letter from 'trip' comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly, meaningless talk or writing, a common informal synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Fraudulent thesis Don concocted

indicators.note: something concocted is made up by mixing ingredients, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A university lecturer faked his doctoral dissertation.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraudulent behaviour involves deceit and cheating, so it is untrustworthy and lacking integrity.

clue.text: Public watched, astonished

parts.note: something public is open to all

explanation.surface: Crowds looked on in amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being amazed makes eyes widen, so wide-eyed with wonder is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Vegetable some reap early

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is taken, lying inside them

parts.note: lies across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A gardener harvests a crop ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round green seed from a pod, eaten as one of the commonest garden crops.

clue.text: Girl meeting posh friend every year

parts.note: U means upper-class in British usage

explanation.surface: A young woman gets together with an upper-class pal once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual events recur once every twelve months, and the adverb describes that yearly frequency.

clue.text: Endless uproar in port

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: Constant tumult in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: The port is Rio de Janeiro in Brazil, commonly shortened to Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian seaport, so the short name is an example of a harbour city.

clue.text: Chooses to include single Conservative in scientific study

indicators.note: including something means holding it within, so one word surrounds the others

explanation.surface: A lone Tory is chosen to join a scientific research project.
explanation.definitionFit: Optics is the branch of physics dealing with light and vision, a field of scientific study.

clue.text: I wondered about cover in retirement

indicators.note: about suggests turning things round and round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has been musing about insurance protection once they stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' looks like giving up work, but here it is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt filled with duck feathers is the bedding that covers you when you retire for the night.

clue.text: US city prosecutors admitting everything

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is let inside another

parts.note: start of DAS, district attorneys, US prosecutors

explanation.surface: Lawyers in an American city making a full confession.
explanation.walkthrough: A DA is a district attorney, the public prosecutor in a US county.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a large city in Texas, so it is an example of an American city.

clue.text: Where you might get blue shoe?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the university where sporting representatives win a Blue
second meaning: a classic laced leather shoe

explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an award for representing Oxford or Cambridge at sport; 'blue shoe' tempts you to look for a coloured shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The university city awards sporting Blues, and a plain lace-up brogue-style shoe also bears the same name.

clue.text: Porridge-maker beginning to overeat at breakfast?

indicators.note: beginning to means just the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: What makes your morning porridge sets you off overindulging at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that breakfast is just one example of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is cooked from ground oats, so this flour or meal is what porridge is made from.

clue.text: All right to go round home making beastly noise?

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

explanation.surface: Is it acceptable to visit someone's house and make horrible noises?
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the setter's pseudonym, Oink, which makes this a little signature.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's grunt is the noise of a beast, so 'beastly' here means made by an animal.

clue.text: One occupying seat in European capital

indicators.note: occupying a place means sitting inside it, so one piece sits within the other

explanation.surface: Someone holds a parliamentary seat in a European capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria, so it is an example of a capital in Europe.

clue.text: Oslo occasionally depressing me a bit

indicators.note: in a down clue, pressing down on something means sitting on top of it in the column
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: The Norwegian capital gets the speaker somewhat down now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Some can mean to a certain degree or somewhat, as in 'it helped some', which is a bit.

clue.text: Ideal position husband found in French resort

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece goes within the other

explanation.surface: A married man finds his perfect spot on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or place that suits someone perfectly, such as finding your niche in life.

clue.text: Mostly respect a Liberal naval officer

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A senior sailor largely respects a Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the highest commanding rank in a navy, so a senior naval officer.
